newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL small-caps end down, blue-chips up slightly.
newsitem.headline: KL small-caps end down, blue-chips up slightly.

text.p: Malaysian small-capitalised stocks continued to take a beating on Monday as punters reaped massive gains made in recent weeks, analysts and dealers said.
Blue-chip stocks rebounded slightly in late trading.
The Second Board index closed down 27.99 points at 567.59, or 4.7 percent, while the benchmark Composite Index was up 4.68 at 1135.27.

Ekran fell 20 cents to 10.80 after investors became nervous over postponement of the signing of the contract between the company, Asea Brown Boveri and Brazil's CBPO for construction of the Bakun hydro-electric dam.
"The Second Board had to slow down sometime," said Ken Loo, head of research at Amsteel Securities. "The recent rise and fall have shown us just how volatile the Second Board can be," he added.
Inspite of the sharp fall on the Second Board, activity was focussed on main board stocks. About 74 percent of the traded shares were on the Main Board of large-capitalised stocks.
Volumes remained high with 223 million shares traded, valued at 1,700 million ringgit.
Losers outnumbered gainers by 456 to 155, while 100 stocks were unchanged.
